The Direct Democracy Cyprus () is a political party in Cyprus established by MEP Fidias Panayiotou. The party was initially named Direct Democracy, but it was renamed to Direct Democracy Cyprus.
As of October 2025, details about the party's structure are limited, with the only confirmed information being that the party's parliamentary candidates will be elected by the public through a mobile app.
The “Agorà” application
The “Agorà” App (meaning “shop” or "marketplace" in modern Greek, also "place of public discussion" in ancient Greek) is the application used by the party supporters to vote on parliamentary issues. The application is expected to become open source after the election of the candidates and the president. After becoming opensource, it is also expected to implement a Zero-knowledge proof of identity by using Eid.
This working app   can be seen by everyone around the world, and in it the Cypriot citizens (by showing their police ID) have the right to vote and indicate to their representative what they want him to vote for. In this way, every parliamentary representative is transformed into a Trojan horse of direct democracy, within a parliamentary environment.
The ultimate goal of such representatives is to become the majority in parliaments and thus transform the widespread political regime of parliamentarism into (direct) democracy.
This is the third attempt to establish direct democracy into a parliament via a similar "Trojan Horse" system, with the first one being IserveU. This idea was also tried, under the name pirategov, in the Pirate Party of Greece from 19 June 2012 until 16 December 2012.
Stances
The party supports direct democracy and e-democracy.
